title: File size validation happens after expensive operations
reasoning: File size validation only applies to non-docx files. For .docx files, there's no size limit before calling file.arrayBuffer() and mammoth.extractRawText(). A malicious or accidental upload of a multi-gigabyte .docx file will load entirely into memory before any processing, potentially freezing the browser or causing OOM crashes. The validation check exempts the exact file type most likely to be large (Word documents with embedded media).
reproduction: 1. Create a 500MB .docx file (embed large images). 2. Upload to DocumentAnalyzerSection. 3. Observe browser freezes while reading entire file into arrayBuffer. 4. May crash on low-memory devices.
recommendation: 1. Apply size limit to ALL file types before reading. Check file.size before arrayBuffer(). 2. Set reasonable limit for .docx (e.g., 10MB). 3. For text extraction, consider streaming or chunked reading if library supports it. 4. Show file size in UI before user uploads to set expectations.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests included. Performance and resource exhaustion issues require load/stress tests with large files.
suggestedRegressionTest: Test: Attempt to upload a >100MB .docx file. Verify size validation rejects before arrayBuffer() call. Verify error message guides user to compress or split file.
minimumFixScope: src/src/pages/BasePortalDemo.tsx analyzeFile function. Apply same fix to DocumentAnalyzerSection in other portal files if pattern is duplicated.
